title: Detecting and Mitigating Subliminal Bias Transmission in LLM Distillation
summary: This paper proposes a method to detect and mitigate the transmission of behavioral traits (e.g., biases) through subliminal learning during LLM distillation. We introduce a framework that identifies hidden signals in synthetic data generated by teacher models and applies counteractive constraints during student model training. The approach is validated by measuring bias amplification in downstream tasks using datasets with known bias baselines, comparing models trained with and without the proposed mitigation.
gap: Ref-014 demonstrates subliminal learning in controlled settings where teacher/student share base models, but does not measure its impact on bias transmission during distillation. No work has measured whether synthetic data generated by biased teacher models amplifies biases in student models during distillation, despite the widespread use of distillation in real-world applications (ref-001, ref-009).
approach: We develop a two-stage process: (1) a statistical analysis of synthetic data using neuron activation patterns correlated with bias metrics (ref-010, ref-014) to detect hidden signals, and (2) a constrained optimization technique during student model training that penalizes the reproduction of these signals via Lagrangian relaxation (ref-012). The method requires teacher/student to share base models (ref-014) and identifies neuron populations responsible for bias transmission through mechanistic interpretability (ref-010).
evaluation: We evaluate using the RealToxicityPrompts dataset (ref-006) and political bias benchmarks (ref-010), comparing bias scores (toxicity, political leaning) of student models trained with/without mitigation. Baselines include standard distillation (ref-009) and adversarial training (ref-006). We isolate the proposed change via ablations: (1) distillation with only statistical analysis of synthetic data, (2) distillation with only mechanistic interpretability for neuron identification, and (3) distillation with only constrained optimization. Success is measured by reduced bias amplification while maintaining task performance (perplexity).
